## How each list was ranked

| Field | Server | Ranking | Server's role in the field | Papers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Psychology | [PsyArXiv](https://psyarxiv.com) | Editorial curation | Useful but partial | 20 |
| Sociology | [SocArXiv](https://osf.io/preprints/socarxiv) | Measured downloads | Small pool | 20 |
| Economics | [SSRN](https://www.ssrn.com) | Partly measured | Right world, wrong pipe | 5 |
| Philosophy | [PhilArchive](https://philarchive.org) | Editorial curation | Journal-driven | 20 |
| Cryptography | [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org) | Editorial curation | Primary venue | 20 |
| Chemistry | [ChemRxiv](https://chemrxiv.org) | Editorial curation | Side channel | 20 |

Only SocArXiv had readable per-paper counts (65 of 100 papers measured). SSRN is partly measured. The other four had no public ranking at all, so their lists are editorial picks — the order is the scout's judgment of impact, not a measured count.

## Signals that can corroborate editorial picks

| Signal | Status | What it is | How to use it |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Altmetric](https://www.altmetric.com/research-access/) | key required | Tracks news, blog, policy and social mentions of DOIs — the best single “did anyone notice this paper” signal. | Every Details Page API request has needed a key since Nov 10, 2025. Free for non-commercial research by application (review targets ~30 business days). The highest-leverage upgrade for the four editorial tabs. |
| [Crossref Event Data](https://crossref.org/blog/strengthening-support-for-data-citations-and-saying-goodbye-to-event-data) | discontinued | Was the free alternative to Altmetric: DOI mentions across blogs, social media, Wikipedia and more. | Retired by Crossref (public API reported gone from April 2026); only a historical archive remains. Not usable for new papers. |
| [OpenAlex](https://openalex.org) | too early | Open scholarly graph with citation counts, successor to Microsoft Academic Graph. | Month-old preprints have essentially no citations, and fresh PsyArXiv DOIs 404'd at scout time. Use it for a 3–6 month retrospective: how did each edition's picks age? |
| [Semantic Scholar API](https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api) | too early | Citation and “influential citation” counts covering papers and preprints. | Same timing problem as OpenAlex; a second opinion on citations for the retrospective. |
| [Sciety](https://sciety.org) | check per paper | eLife-built aggregator of community peer evaluations of preprints from dozens of review groups. | Look up individual picks; an evaluation or curation statement is independent corroboration. PsyArXiv coverage not confirmed. |
| [PREreview](https://prereview.org) | check per paper | Open, ORCID-signed preprint reviews with DOIs. | Explicitly supports PsyArXiv, SocArXiv, OSF, medRxiv and bioRxiv. A published review of a pick is strong corroboration. |
| [OSF API](https://api.osf.io/v2/) | enumeration | Lists every PsyArXiv and SocArXiv preprint in a window. | Gives completeness, not ranking: no view/download counters are exposed. Per-page counters (which exclude the authors' own views) render only in the browser. OSF's generalist server has paused new submissions since Aug 25, 2025; community servers such as PsyArXiv and SocArXiv are unaffected. |
| [Crossref REST API](https://api.crossref.org) | enumeration | Lists every ChemRxiv preprint (DOI prefix 10.26434) and verifies authors/dates. | Rate-limits under load (HTTP 429). Space requests out; the 7 unverified chemistry papers need exactly this. |

## Finding more servers

To scout a new field, start from a directory of preprint servers rather than a chart of posting volume.

- [SPI-Hub preprint service browser](https://spi-hub.app.vumc.org/pp-service/browse) — Searchable directory of preprint servers with scope and policy details — the fastest way to find a field's servers.
- [ASAPbio Preprint Resource Center](https://asapbio.org/focus-areas/preprints/preprint-resource-center/) — Guides and server listings from the preprint-advocacy nonprofit ASAPbio. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [COS: community servers on OSF stay active](https://www.cos.io/blog/suspension-of-submissions-to-generalist-preprint-server-for-review-and-next-steps-community-servers-hosted-by-osf-preprints-remain-active) — Why OSF's generalist server paused submissions (Aug 2025) while PsyArXiv, SocArXiv and other community servers continue.

## By field

### Psychology — PsyArXiv

**Ranking:** Editorial curation · **Role in the field:** Useful but partial

**Why:** No public download ranking exists. OSF's API exposes no view/download counters (verified in the raw JSON), the metrics endpoints 404, and Altmetric now needs an API key.

**How the list was picked:** All 1,222 PsyArXiv preprints from Sep 18–Oct 18, 2026 were enumerated via the OSF API. The 20 below are an editorial ranking by estimated impact — landmark formats (consensus statements, megastudies, large meta-analyses, preregistered reports), data scale, novelty, and subfield diversity — not a measured leaderboard.

**Where the field publishes:** PsyArXiv carries a lot of psychology, but high-profile work often appears journal-first, clinical psychology and psychiatry often go to medRxiv, and cognitive neuroscience to bioRxiv.

**Corroborate these picks**

- [PREreview](https://prereview.org) — Open reviews of PsyArXiv preprints — a review of a pick is independent quality evidence.
- [Sciety](https://sciety.org) — Aggregated community evaluations; check picks individually.
- [BPS Research Digest](https://www.bps.org.uk/research-digest) — British Psychological Society write-ups of notable new studies. *(description not yet re-checked)*

**Look beyond PsyArXiv**

- [medRxiv — Psychiatry & Clinical Psychology](https://www.medrxiv.org/collection/psychiatry-and-clinical-psychology) — Where much clinical psychology preprints instead of PsyArXiv. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [bioRxiv — Neuroscience](https://www.biorxiv.org/collection/neuroscience) — Cognitive and affective neuroscience preprints. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Nature Human Behaviour](https://www.nature.com/nathumbehav/) — Top general-audience behavioural science journal. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Psychological Science](https://journals.sagepub.com/home/pss) — APS flagship empirical journal. *(description not yet re-checked)*

### Sociology — SocArXiv

**Ranking:** Measured downloads · **Role in the field:** Small pool

**Why:** Ranked by REAL per-paper download counts. Each OSF preprint page shows public view/download counters; 65 of the 100 papers in-window were measured (a 429 rate limit stopped the sweep). No public trending page or metrics API exists.

**How the list was picked:** All 100 SocArXiv preprints from Sep 18–Oct 18, 2026 pulled via the OSF API; each page's counters read Oct 18. Sorted by downloads desc, ties by views. Partial ranking — 35 papers unmeasured, and earlier papers had more days to accumulate downloads.

**Where the field publishes:** SocArXiv posts only ~100 papers a month; most sociology goes straight to journals (ASR, AJS). Political science overlaps heavily — this edition's #1 sociology paper is an IR study.

**Corroborate these picks**

- [SocArXiv per-paper counters](https://osf.io/preprints/socarxiv) — Each preprint page shows public view/download counters (contributors' own views excluded) — the basis of this tab's ranking; re-read them to fill the 35 unmeasured papers.
- [PREreview](https://prereview.org) — Supports SocArXiv; check picks for open reviews.
- [SocArXiv blog (SocOpen)](https://socopen.org) — Server news and aggregate submission counts (no per-paper rankings).

**Look beyond SocArXiv**

- [APSA Preprints](https://preprints.apsanet.org) — American Political Science Association's server (hosted by Cambridge) — natural partner if politics counts, or a candidate seventh tab.
- [Sociological Science](https://sociologicalscience.com) — Fast, open-access general sociology journal. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [American Sociological Review](https://journals.sagepub.com/home/asr) — ASA flagship journal. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [IZA Discussion Papers](https://www.iza.org/publications/dp) — Labor, family and demography working papers that sociologists read. *(description not yet re-checked)*

### Economics — SSRN

**Ranking:** Partly measured · **Role in the field:** Right world, wrong pipe

**Why:** SSRN sunset its download rankings on July 15, 2026 — the Top Papers leaderboards are gone permanently. Per-paper download counts still show on individual abstract pages, but nothing aggregates them.

**How the list was picked:** Candidates drawn from NBER weekly releases Sep 18–Oct 18, 2026 (nearly all cross-posted to SSRN). Only 5 could be verified with a live SSRN abstract page in-window — fresh SSRN pages aren't search-indexed yet. Ordered by per-page downloads where visible. A retry in a week or two should fill out the 20.

**Where the field publishes:** Economics runs on working papers, but SSRN's rankings are gone and fresh SSRN pages index slowly. RePEc indexes NBER, CEPR, IZA, the Fed series and SSRN-adjacent work, and still publishes measured download rankings.

**Corroborate these picks**

- [LogEc (RePEc)](https://logec.repec.org) — Real monthly download and abstract-view counts across IDEAS, EconPapers and NEP; CSV export via format=csv. Can restore a measured ranking to this tab.
- [IDEAS rankings](https://ideas.repec.org/top/) — RePEc's ranking pages, including top items by recent downloads, refreshed early each month.
- [NEP: New Economics Papers](https://nep.repec.org) — 90+ weekly field reports, each human-edited from the 500–1,000 new papers that week — independent curation per subfield.

**Look beyond SSRN**

- [NBER Working Papers](https://www.nber.org/papers) — This tab's current candidate pool; nearly all cross-post to SSRN.
- [CEPR Discussion Papers](https://cepr.org/publications/discussion-papers) — Europe's equivalent of the NBER series. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Federal Reserve FEDS working papers](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/feds/index.htm) — Fed Board research series (macro, finance). *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [VoxEU columns](https://cepr.org/voxeu) — Researcher-written summaries — a column about a paper is a signal it matters. *(description not yet re-checked)*

### Philosophy — PhilArchive

**Ranking:** Editorial curation · **Role in the field:** Journal-driven

**Why:** No public stats source exists. Download counts are tracked but shown only to authors; no most-downloaded page, no public API, no per-item public counts.

**How the list was picked:** Drawn from PhilArchive's “Selected recent additions” feed (the archive's own quality-filtered list). The public feed caps at 100 items, so coverage is Oct 12–18 only. Ranked by venue prestige, author prominence, novelty, and area diversity — editorial judgment, not metrics.

**Where the field publishes:** PhilArchive is the open-access archive inside PhilPapers, which indexes far more (new journal issues included). The real quality signal in philosophy is journal acceptance — most of this edition's picks already have one.

**Corroborate these picks**

- [Journal acceptance](https://philpapers.org) — The venue shown on each card is refereed peer judgment; PhilPapers tracks journals' new and forthcoming issues.
- [The Philosopher's Annual](https://philosophersannual.org) — Selects the ten best articles of each year (45th edition, for 2025, announced Aug 2026) — a yearly check on the picks.
- [Daily Nous](https://dailynous.com) — Profession news; occasional reader threads on very good recent articles.

**Look beyond PhilArchive**

- [PhilPapers](https://philpapers.org) — Superset of PhilArchive; “Monitor current research” shows recent additions across journals.
- [PhilArchive — Selected recent additions](https://philarchive.org/recent.html?filter=1) — This tab's current pool (capped at 100 items, so only ~a week deep).
- [SEP — What's New](https://plato.stanford.edu/new.html) — New and revised Stanford Encyclopedia entries. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Philosophers' Imprint](https://journals.publishing.umich.edu/phimp/) — Leading open-access general philosophy journal. *(description not yet re-checked)*

### Cryptography — IACR ePrint

**Ranking:** Editorial curation · **Role in the field:** Primary venue

**Why:** No current download ranking exists — IACR's last “Top 20 Downloads” reports were in 2010–2011 newsletters. The archive publishes submission counts per year only.

**How the list was picked:** Every listing Sep 18–Oct 18, 2026 (ePrint 2026/2060–2522) was read; 24 nominated, ranked to 20 by: (1) breaks on deployed systems or standards-track PQC, (2) new primitives/models, (3) major efficiency gains, (4) notable teams/community pickup, (5) subfield diversity. ePrint is unrefereed — attack claims are as-claimed.

**Where the field publishes:** ePrint is the field's own preprint archive — the right source. Quality is decided at the top conferences, and a lot of security work posts only to arXiv cs.CR, which the beyond-arXiv premise excludes.

**Corroborate these picks**

- [IACR conferences](https://iacr.org/meetings/) — CRYPTO, Eurocrypt, Asiacrypt and area conferences — later acceptance is the field's quality stamp. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [NIST PQC forum](https://groups.google.com/a/list.nist.gov/g/pqc-forum) — Where attacks on candidate schemes (MAYO, SNOVA, Falcon, ML-KEM) get discussed and vetted. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [IACR news feed](https://iacr.org/news/) — Reposts new ePrint papers automatically (ePrint Report channel), so a listing is not an endorsement — useful only to see what's new.
- [IACR Communications in Cryptology](https://cic.iacr.org) — IACR's diamond open-access journal; acceptance there corroborates an ePrint paper.

**Look beyond IACR ePrint**

- [ePrint RSS feeds](https://eprint.iacr.org/rss) — Publication-date-ordered feeds — the easiest way to enumerate a window.
- [arXiv cs.CR](https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CR/recent) — Security and privacy preprints that skip ePrint (outside this digest's premise, but where much applied security lands). *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [USENIX Security](https://www.usenix.org/conferences/byname/108) — Top systems-security venue; accepted-paper lists corroborate applied attacks. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [ACM CCS](https://www.sigsac.org/ccs.html) — Top-tier security conference. *(description not yet re-checked)*

### Chemistry — ChemRxiv

**Ranking:** Editorial curation · **Role in the field:** Side channel

**Why:** Article pages show public “N views / M downloads”, but pages are bot-blocked (403) and there is no sortable, date-filtered, or API-exposed ranking. The dashboard's Most read/Most cited are all-time only.

**How the list was picked:** All 1,431 ChemRxiv preprints in-window enumerated via the Crossref API; every title scanned. Editorial ranking on novelty, potential impact, and subfield mix. 19 of 20 now have verified authors and dates; #17's Crossref record lists no authors — flagged inline.

**Where the field publishes:** Most top chemistry goes straight to journals (JACS, Angewandte, Nature Chemistry) and many groups never preprint. ChemRxiv shows a slice; editorial highlight services are a better guide to what mattered.

**Corroborate these picks**

- [C&EN](https://cen.acs.org) — ACS news magazine; covers notable new results, including preprints. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Chemistry World](https://www.chemistryworld.com) — RSC news magazine; research news coverage of notable papers. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Synfacts](https://www.thieme.de/en/synfacts/journal-information-55968.htm) — Monthly expert-selected highlights of new synthesis results with commentary.
- [ChemRxiv per-paper counts](https://chemrxiv.org/engage/chemrxiv/public-dashboard) — Each article page shows views/downloads to human readers (bots get 403); a slow manual pass can test the 20 picks.

**Look beyond ChemRxiv**

- [JACS — Just Accepted / ASAP](https://pubs.acs.org/toc/jacsat/0/0) — Newest JACS papers, the field's flagship. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Angewandte Chemie](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/15213773) — Leading European general chemistry journal. *(description not yet re-checked)*
- [Nature Chemistry](https://www.nature.com/nchem/) — High-impact general chemistry journal. *(description not yet re-checked)*

## Using these on a weekly run

1. Enumerate the window from the primary server (OSF API, Crossref, ePrint RSS, PhilArchive feed, NBER/RePEc).
2. Where a measured ranking exists (SocArXiv counters, SSRN page counts, LogEc), use it and say so.
3. Otherwise pick editorially and write the criteria into the report's `method:` front matter.
4. For each pick, look for at least one corroborating signal from the lists above and add it under the paper:

   ```
   3. [Title](https://...) — Authors — Oct 12 — Note.
      - corroboration: [C&EN story](https://...) · PREreview · Altmetric 140
   ```

5. Run `python3 build_html.py --check` and `--check-links`, then build.

## Planned improvements

1. **Economics: rank with LogEc.** Pull candidates from RePEc (NBER, CEPR, IZA, Fed series) and rank by LogEc downloads. Restores a measured ranking to the tab SSRN broke.
2. **Apply for an Altmetric research key.** Free for non-commercial research; ~30 business days. Adds an attention score to every pick in every tab.
3. **Keep the corroboration pass weekly.** First pass done Oct 18, 2026 (evidence lines on each card, Notable elsewhere lists). Repeat it each week and re-check the editions' picks for new coverage, venue acceptances and corrections.
4. **Filter by first-posted date.** OSF counts a new version as a new posting; 8 psychology and 2 sociology picks in the first edition were revisions of older preprints. Enumerate by each preprint's first version date.
5. **Fill first-edition gaps.** Verify the 7 ChemRxiv authors via Crossref, retry SSRN/NBER candidates, measure the 35 unmeasured SocArXiv papers.
6. **Decide on politics.** Either a seventh tab from APSA Preprints or fold political science into Sociology.
7. **Retrospective at 3–6 months.** Re-score each edition's picks with OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar citations and publish how the editorial picks aged.
